data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between truly independent and hidden correlated failures is identified by the 'Temporal Signature' of the failure onset: Poisson-distributed arrivals vs. trigger-based synchronization.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The common cause is a 'slow-burn' trigger that activates based on local state rather than a global timestamp.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The network is so small that the sample size of failures is insufficient to distinguish a Poisson process from a clustered one.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Truly independent failures are caused by stochastic, local events (e.g., hardware wear), resulting in a Poisson distribution of failure timestamps.
